steps.note: Reflection prompts only; no selection and no grant.

decisions.quote: The first thing you should do is think about the kind of hero you want to make.
Choose your hero's humanoid ancestry from among the range of ancestries available in the game
Unless otherwise noted, a character of any of these ancestries is size 1M and has speed 5 and stability 0.
decisions.note: Absent from en/unified/md/chapter/ancestries.md; present only in the clean Heroes text.

decisions.quote: Each ancestry has one or more signature traits, which your hero gets for free if they take that ancestry.
You have one skill of your choice from the interpersonal skill group
You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits.

budgetRule.quote: But they couldn't select both Impressive Horns and Wings, since their combined cost of 4 exceeds the ancestry points budget for the devil.

steps.note: A culture is assembled from four aspects: language, environment, organization, upbringing. The culture's name and description are authored text.

decisions.quote: Choose or create your hero's culture.
All player characters know Caelian!
You know the language of your culture, in addition to knowing Caelian.
When you build a culture, select its environment aspect from the following options: nomadic, rural, secluded, urban, or wilderness.
You can select one skill from each aspect's list of options.

Nomadic.quote: One skill from the exploration or interpersonal skill groups.

Rural.quote: One skill from the crafting or lore skill groups.

Secluded.quote: One skill from the interpersonal or lore skill groups.

Urban.quote: One skill from the interpersonal or intrigue skill groups.

Wilderness.quote: One skill from the crafting or exploration skill groups.

decisions.quote: When you build a culture, select its organization aspect from the following options: bureaucratic or communal.
You can select one skill from each aspect's list of options.

Bureaucratic.quote: One skill from the interpersonal or intrigue skill groups.

Communal.quote: One skill from the crafting or exploration skill groups.

decisions.quote: Pick your upbringing aspect from the following list: academic, creative, labor, lawless, martial, or noble.
You can select one skill from each aspect's list of options.

Academic.quote: One skill from the lore skill group.

Creative.quote: The Music or Perform skill (from the interpersonal skill group), or one skill from the crafting group.

Labor.quote: The Blacksmithing skill (from the crafting skill group), the Handle Animals skill (from the interpersonal group), or a skill from the exploration group.

Lawless.quote: One skill from the intrigue skill group.

Martial.quote: One of the following: Blacksmithing or Fletching from the crafting skill group; Climb, Endurance, or Ride from the exploration group; Intimidate from the interpersonal group; Alertness or Track from the intrigue group; or Monsters or Strategy from the lore skill group

Noble.quote: One skill from the interpersonal skill group.

decisions.quote: You gain an edge on tests made to recall lore about your culture, and on tests made to influence and interact with people of your culture.

grants.value: edge on culture lore and culture interaction tests (manual in v0.01)

decisions.quote: Choose your hero's career, which describes what you did for a living before you became a hero.
decisions.note: Sub-decisions below are defined for Soldier only (the v0.01 supported career). Every other career defines its own skills, languages, perk type, Renown, wealth and project-point grants and inciting-incident table in its entry; V08 expands them.

decisions.quote: One skill from the exploration skill group and one skill from the intrigue group
One skill from the exploration skill group and one skill from the intrigue group
Languages: Two languages

deferralRule.quote: You can choose to leave some of the languages you know open until you discover what might be a good choice for the campaign you're playing in.

poolRule.quote: Some careers allow you to learn extra languages, chosen from those available in Languages in Orden above.

decisions.quote: Renown: +1

baseRule.quote: At the start of character creation, your Renown is 0.

decisions.quote: Perk: One exploration perk

typeRule.quote: Whenever a feature allows you to gain a perk, that feature tells you which type of perk to choose.

decisions.quote: Inciting Incident

choiceRule.quote: You can roll for or choose an inciting incident from the table that accompanies each career.

decisions.note: A unique incident authored with the Director is source-permitted (background.md: "come up with a unique inciting incident of your own") and is deliberately not supported in v0.01.

decisions.quote: Record what was taken from you on your character sheet, and let your Director know.
You can be a censor, conduit, elementalist, fury, null, shadow, tactician, talent, or troubadour.
Each option you can choose for your hero at 1st level includes a parenthetical selection labeled "Quick Build."
decisions.note: v0.01 creates at level one only (docs/character-wizard-spec.md#v001-scope).

decisions.quote: You start with a Might of 2 and an Agility of 2
you can choose one of the following arrays for your other characteristic scores:
for your other characteristic scores
decisions.note: The source does not state whether the array values may be assigned to Reason, Intuition and Presence in any order.

decisions.quote: Starting Stamina at 1st Level: 21

grants.value: Weak Potency: Might − 2; Average Potency: Might − 1; Strong Potency: Might

decisions.quote: You gain the Nature skill
Then choose any two skills from the exploration or intrigue skill groups.
Primordial Aspect, Ferocity, Growing Ferocity, Aspect Features, Aspect Triggered Action, Mighty Leaps, Fury Abilities
You choose a primordial aspect from the following options, each of which grants you a skill.

featureRule.quote: Your primordial aspect grants you two features, as shown on the 1st-Level Aspect Features table.

triggeredRule.quote: Your primordial aspect grants you a triggered action, as shown on the Aspect Triggered Actions table.

decisions.quote: Choose one signature ability from the following options.

poolSource.note: The unified feature entry omits the option list; membership is taken from the ability headings under Signature Ability in the clean Heroes text and the ability entries' missing cost field.

decisions.quote: Choose one heroic ability from the following options, each of which costs 3 ferocity to use.
Choose one heroic ability from the following options, each of which costs 5 ferocity to use.
You can use and gain the benefits of a kit.

stepRule.quote: Your class might grant your hero a kit that helps define your approach to martial combat.

Stormwight.quote: You can use and gain the benefits of a stormwight kit

decisions.quote: You wear heavy armor and wield a heavy weapon.
decisions.note: References for R02; every kit entry carries its own bonuses and signature ability in the same shape.

decisions.quote: Every hero has a melee weapon free strike and a ranged weapon free strike.
decisions.note: The narrative description of what the free strikes are is authored text; kit modifiers are R02.

steps.optionalQuote: complications aren't necessary for making a great hero

decisions.quote: You can choose your character's complication from any of the available options below.
decisions.note: Not presented in v0.01 (Q-CHAR-1 answered 2026-09-14: no). The pool is recorded by reference only; individual complications are not listed here.

it's time to determine the additional details of their backstory, appearance, and personality.
